overview: File documents Taiwan's August 1941 alien-control revision under Ordinance No. 153, with Bruner confirming consular staff remain exempt, through despatch, translation, and acknowledgment.

people.name: Glen Bruner
people.role: American Vice Consul at Taihoku, Taiwan

people.name: Teruo Hachiya
people.role: Chief of the Department of Foreign Affairs, Government-General of Taiwan

subfiles.title: Despatch from Bruner to Grew concerning revised alien-control regulations
subfiles.from: Glen Bruner, American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Bruner reports that Taiwan’s revised alien-control ordinance does not apply to foreign consular personnel, their families, or their employees.
subfiles.summary: Bruner reports Taiwan's revised alien-control rules keep consular staff and families exempt, enclosing translation and reply.

subfiles.title: Translation of Government-General notification on Ordinance No. 153
subfiles.from: Teruo Hachiya, Chief of the Department of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: The Government-General formally notifies the American Consul of the revised alien-control ordinance and confirms the continuing consular exemption.
subfiles.summary: Translation: Taiwan's Ordinance No. 153 revises alien-control rules but still exempts foreign consular staff and families.

subfiles.title: Bruner’s acknowledgment to Teruo Hachiya
subfiles.to: Teruo Hachiya, Chief of the Department of Foreign Affairs, Government-General of Taiwan
subfiles.about: Bruner acknowledges the colonial government’s notification and expresses thanks for confirming the exemption of consular personnel.
subfiles.summary: Bruner acknowledges Taiwan's confirmation that consular staff remain exempt under the revised alien ordinance.

interest: Shows Taiwan's 1941 revised alien-control rules preserving consular exemptions, just before Pearl Harbor.
